chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Salama, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Fasting the month of Sha'ban and the month of Ramadan consecutively is an expiation (or act of repentance) from Allah, the Exalted.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.رَمَضَان: Ramadan (the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, known for fasting)
key_terms.شَعْبَان: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of fasting in Sha'ban before Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the continuous fasting of Sha'ban and Ramadan as a means of expiation (kaffarah) for sins. This practice is historically significant as it reflects the pre-Ramadan spiritual preparation emphasized in Shia tradition, linking voluntary devotion with the obligatory fasts to secure divine forgiveness.
